rites.name: Vausum
rites.text: A long-retired kind of spellcaster whose craft once appeared among the cards of a traveling deck. Its old form is now considered outdated and no longer used.

rites.name: Seorus Teliasonia
rites.text: A prepackaged hunting arrangement of beasts and growth-charms, bound to a wild commander. Its fixed core cannot be stripped away, though new spoils can be woven into it over time.

rites.name: Ameres
rites.text: A set of five binding sigils that are inscribed upon a creature to shield it from one particular elemental hue. Each mark is worn only by the creature it was etched upon.

rites.name: Varneollus
rites.text: A tally of injury that has been stored away, able to be turned back into living strength. Practitioners keep these reserves as a measure of recovery waiting to be drawn upon.

rites.name: Viarnium
rites.text: A binding rite that fuses a beast's spirit with a person's spirit into one calm being. Those who accept it become loyal, peaceful servants, and some are fully freed from their affliction.

rites.name: Riarnium
rites.text: A warrior's discipline that swells a fighter's strength whenever they stand against an opponent or are met in combat. The effect rises as the duel joins.

rites.name: Amonentium
rites.text: A binding craft that breathes will into inert matter, letting a lifeless object rise and act as a living thing for a stretch of time before it settles again.

rites.name: Valirnor
rites.text: A ritual hunger that wakes in a warrior when they draw blood from a rival, feeding their body with growing might. Each strike that finds a foe's flesh leaves the bearer a little stronger.

rites.name: Lises
rites.text: A lingering enchantment that binds a being in place so it cannot regain its readiness. The effect is known among scholars of the arcane as a quiet, creeping drain.

rites.name: Orirostum
rites.text: A clash where one bearer drives its strength into a chosen foe, dealing harm equal to its own might. The strike arrives without any answering blow from the target.

rites.name: Tonelles
rites.text: A ritual gift that lets a sacred spirit be bound to a mortal vessel, lending its strength, endurance, and powers to whatever it is joined with.

rites.name: Naullium
rites.text: A bonding craft in which allied helpers lend their bodies to a caster's working, tapping into the group's shared strength. Its origins trace to a guild of green-clad communal keepers.

rites.name: Coralenum
rites.text: A craft by which harm is dealt to a chosen being or stronghold without any clash of arms, carried instead by a bolt of pure arcane force.

rites.name: Teleraurnes
rites.text: A rare binding that lets one wielder take over a whole participant, directing that person's choices and deeds as though they were a held object.

rites.name: Raustia
rites.text: A ritual contest of opposing forces that a practitioner may invoke. It was first recorded among the forest peoples and later revived in a second age of the same tradition.

rites.name: Rauntum
rites.text: A preserving rite named for its wrapping of the dead, letting a fallen body be cloned into a new form. It belongs to the white and blue crafts of sealing and renewal.

rites.name: Corernilia
rites.text: A bond where a leader gathers followers into a group that can share the blows taken in battle. Once joined, the group changes how attacks and defenses are made, though the old practice has since been set aside.

rites.name: Corollintus
rites.text: A devotional craft in which worshippers pledge their faith to one or two elemental hues. The number of marks gathered in these pledges is counted to empower the rites of a temple's patron deity.

rites.name: Vineostanum
rites.text: A temple-taught practice where a bearer taps a stone and grants another creature a timed surge of strength and endurance until the turn ends.

rites.name: Teleonistor
rites.text: A bound quality that keeps a creature from ever striking outward, so it can only stand guard and block. It is a lasting, unchanging trait rather than an action.

rites.name: Ninteostium
rites.text: A tunneling evasion craft that lets a creature slip past foes who would otherwise strike from above. Those wielding wings cannot stop such a delver from passing beneath their reach.

rites.name: Nalirum
rites.text: A bound servant-form that fights on a keeper's behalf, marching out each cycle to strike foes or hold the line against their advance. Most keepers rely on such bound forms as the core of their war-plans.

rites.name: Mellantium
rites.text: A working that can be woven without drawing on any reserve of power. Such workings usually carry a different price paid in another form.

rites.name: Rirus
rites.text: A lone warrior who strikes without companions is strengthened by each sacred sigil marked upon the field under one's command, growing bolder with every blessing shining above the battle.

rites.name: Vostauntus
rites.text: A triggered rite that stirs a creature into a fury whenever it is struck. It belongs to the great reptile beasts of a sun-worshipping empire.

rites.name: Corarostia
rites.text: A sealing working once woven across an entire land, binding the dark and blood-touched beings within it so they could not wound one another. Its unraveling opened the realm to outside raiders.

rites.name: Tonus
rites.text: A lasting charm woven into the world that stays in force indefinitely once it takes hold. It is a standing kind of sorcery, carried into the present by those who learned how to bind it.

rites.name: Sereorallum
rites.text: A bound oath laid upon a warrior people, forbidding them to strike any foe greater than their own strength. Instead they withdraw to study their rivals, which over time makes them the mightiest of their kind.

rites.name: Renes Vaurus
rites.text: A deliberate strain of effort that a creature can choose to spend, marking it as worn for later. Practitioners of the old temple disciplines favor it in their crafts of resolve and force.

rites.name: Teleostanum
rites.text: A preserved rite that lets a fallen card rise again from its resting place as a bound, embalmed servant. The art is tied to a sealed order of revenants stitched together with a glittering binding salve.

rites.name: Valasontor
rites.text: A common binding craft that lets a caster seize full command of lesser beings they call or summon. A truly unyielding mind can loosen or shatter the hold.

rites.name: Siarum
rites.text: A brief enchantment that is never set in place among the wards. Once its cost is paid and its effect unfolds, it is immediately sent to the caster's resting pile.

rites.name: Vialeosium
rites.text: A one-time magical working that is cast and then resolves, much like a quick incantation. It belongs with other brief enchantments that take effect for a short span.

rites.name: Milliastia
rites.text: A small cycle of five swift incantations, each able to alter a chosen spell or object so that it takes on a single hue. Their power is drawn quickly, at moments of interruption.

rites.name: Riastanum
rites.text: A practitioner calls a creature from elsewhere to come forth and serve their command. The craft binds the summoned being to follow the caller's will.

rites.name: Tarium Corneostum
rites.text: A bond that joins two of a warrior's companions into a single pair. Once paired, the companions fight alongside each other and share their strength.

rites.name: Cauntes
rites.text: A practiced art in which a caster who has stored two or more quick incantations or sealed rites in their remembrance gains altered or added properties to their working.

rites.name: Vaullus
rites.text: A ritual craft in which a bound relic is drawn back up out of the grave for a single brief use. Practitioners of the shadowed guilds treasure it above nearly all else.

rites.name: Vonaures
rites.text: A shared mind woven between the members of a folk, letting their thoughts flow together as one communal awareness. Its linked minds also bind the group into a single sensing whole.

rites.name: Valor
rites.text: A deadly quality that lets any strike touching a creature end its life outright. Old keepers of the craft record it on many ancient charms.

rites.name: Amarnollium
rites.text: A tally that marks a warrior-in-training as they are shaped into a disciplined fighter by a patient mentor. Each mark records a step toward a code of honor.

rites.name: Ilotamira
rites.text: Ilotamira is the concept of the Seeding in Orierlae, the quiet hour when the makers plant the Weave and the sleeping powers of the Arcane Realm are first bound into the land. It is less a force than a stillness that lets threads of power settle without waking.

rites.name: Ilyennora
rites.text: Ilyennora is a concept of the Weave, the quiet web of power that the makers plant in the Seeding of Orierlae, when sovereign groves first take root. It is not a being but an idea that gives shape to growing kingdoms and the sleeping powers within them. Its strength lies in what it allows others to grow into.

rites.name: Miaranum
rites.text: A watchful gift borne by certain beings, letting them strike forward while keeping their guard raised and ready to defend.

rites.name: Orales
rites.text: A dark practice in which a caster tears vitality from a rival and binds it into their own body. Sinister circles favor it, and some lesser schools dabble in its quieter forms.

rites.name: Corilor
rites.text: A cunning trade of worth, where a caster surrenders a bound relic, a sealed charm, or a conjured wisp as the working is spoken, gaining an added boon in return.

rites.name: Ciallum
rites.text: A tally that grows with heated conditions and strikes harm in proportion to the fire it measures. Practitioners use it to reckon the burn of a moment.

rites.name: Sineria
rites.text: A ritual craft in which a warrior's rage is fed by spilled blood, granting a surge of strength to those who draw it. It is practiced by a wild, lawless brotherhood of raiders.

rites.name: Coreostia Lirnium
rites.text: A practiced craft that lets a bearer trade a bound charm of enchantment for a different charm held in their palm. The exchange happens at the moment the charm is invoked.

rites.name: Seoniranum
rites.text: A practice where a keeper peers at the uppermost few lots of a hidden cache and claims one bearing a chosen trait. It was first named after a verdant rite of the forest folk.

rites.name: Orialintes
rites.text: A green-white craft in which enchanting spellcasters draw many cards whenever their charm-like magics take hold. Earlier practitioners pushed quick attacks, while later ones bounced everything to lock rivals out.

rites.name: Corasialor
rites.text: A recurring craft that is passed along to newcomers during a certain age of its world. Its effects appear only among those who first learned it there.

rites.name: Nentium Oreolasum
rites.text: A practiced art of drawing heat and flame out of the body to shape fire at will. Its wielders are typically marked as members of a distinct tradition of combat and control.

rites.name: Sonus
rites.text: A recurring craft of five spellwork rites, bound to a school of ancient sorcery. Its purpose is to answer what it means for a short incantation to carry the weight of legend.

rites.name: Ninteollum
rites.text: A bracing craft that lets a bulwark be set upon a holding. It works like fitting a gear to a fighter, but the anchor is the ground itself rather than a warrior.

rites.name: Nernases
rites.text: A protective warding craft that keeps a bearer from being singled out by rival sorcerers or their enchantments. The ward lasts for as long as its bearer endures.

rites.name: Oreoroses
rites.text: A binding craft that seals a bearer's chosen object in stillness, so it cannot rouse when its keeper next wakes. Its sign is a cold rime frosting the sealed thing.

rites.name: Coses
rites.text: A quiet working that drifts over a battlefield and smothers every blow struck during one passing round. Several schools of the craft carry it under different guises, each forcing harm aside.

rites.name: Rosaustor
rites.text: A deceptive power where a creature must be given up whenever a spell is aimed at it. Older forms of this power also reacted to other magical effects, and later designs react only to spells.

rites.name: Tistus
rites.text: A ritual of mixing a stack of cards until its order is wholly unpredictable. It may only be performed when the governing rules call for it, and practitioners blend folding and stacking motions.

rites.name: Laustum
rites.text: A binding craft that lets a bearer fuse its power onto a spell being cast, adding a lesser effect from one arcane instant. It draws on the instant's own might.

rites.name: Meornorium
rites.text: A rite that lets the caster pick one of several distinct workings when it is invoked. Each chosen working is a separate option the caster may select.

rites.name: Teliseornor
rites.text: A quiet art of slipping past notice that a creature can carry into battle. It keeps the creature out of reach of those who would strike back.

rites.name: Visum Valaunium
rites.text: A long-running stratagem where a creature is laid to rest in a deathyard, then roused back into the fight by a cheap incantation. Its practitioners have relied on this method since the earliest days of the contest.

rites.name: Tornor
rites.text: A banished beast is replaced on the field by a random creature drawn from its owner's deck, which the owner reveals from the top of their supply until one turns up.

rites.name: Seraunum Leosanum
rites.text: A signal-mark that alerts certain effects whenever a ground-tile arrives on the field under its keeper's command. The mark calls those responding effects into action at that moment.

rites.name: Mauntanum
rites.text: A hidden ward that only springs when a quick, fleeting working is cast. Its craft first arose in a wild, untamed land and later reappeared in another region.

rites.name: Coroleontor
rites.text: A ground that yields an effect beyond gathering power. Its hidden craft may unmake standing things, bolster creatures, or empty a deck, often by drawing on the ground itself or its neighbors.

rites.name: Sentiarum Valeolia
rites.text: A coined keyword marking a bargain whose bait lures opponents into accepting it. It is found only on quick spells and instant tricks, never on lasting works.

rites.name: Teollanum Serintales
rites.text: A bold tactic lets an attacker turn unblocked strikes aside, sending their force against a chosen foe rather than the waiting ruler. It is spoken of in rough street talk among cunning captains.

rites.name: Viraulor
rites.text: A spell-quality that keeps a working from being unraveled by rival magic. Scribes write it into the binding text as a plain prohibition against undoing the casting.

rites.name: Sintiares
rites.text: A craft of hardening raw beasts through repeated practice, found only among creatures that can be shaped by discipline and effort.

rites.name: Lyemeth
rites.text: Lyemeth is a concept in Orierlae, the principle of growth that the first sovereign drew upon when the worlds broke apart during the Sundering. It is remembered in the groves as the force that stitched the Shards back toward one another under the Pact. Its later forms are named only in the oldest songs of the growing kingdoms.

rites.name: Cernillum
rites.text: A fast strategy built on many cheap, efficient light-aligned fighters that often slip past blockers. Its users aim to strike hard and quickly, sometimes boosting their attackers with lasting blessings.

rites.name: Miarnantes
rites.text: A set of three hues made of one hue and the two rivals opposite it, forming a sharp triangular pattern. Its counterpart is a pairing of one hue with its two allies.

rites.name: Neostes
rites.text: A turning craft in which every seeker discards their gathered hand and draws a fresh set of seven tokens. Many forms exist, though the practice now survives mainly in one line of its tradition.

rites.name: Nostus
rites.text: A tally of courage that gathers on bearers in the field. Each marked bearer grows a little stronger for every token of bravery bound to the one who carries it.

rites.name: Maulum
rites.text: A tactic in which a single chosen warrior is raised by gathering charms and armor upon it until it becomes a dangerous force against rivals.

rites.name: Leores
rites.text: A tally of three spent sparks that bearers burn to call a chosen treasure from a sealed archive. Each burn answers one of three unspoken requests.

rites.name: Tasornum
rites.text: A guiding power drawn from open plains that upholds balance and order. It values the common good above private greed, and it shields its allies with many small defenders and lawful protections.

rites.name: Siantia
rites.text: A battlefield craft in which a being's strength and endurance rise with every companion it commands. It began among fiery raiders and later spread to rallying armies that reward large numbers of small followers.

rites.name: Telaustia
rites.text: A keyless tide of magic that a leader's repeated summoning from a safe reserve can multiply. Each return from that reserve lets a spell echo itself into duplicates.

rites.name: Cintasia
rites.text: A standing trait woven into a thing that quietly declares its nature, such as its kin-lineage or lack of hue, and it holds true whether the thing is in use or set aside.

rites.name: Telontium
rites.text: A dark current drawn from fenland rot that teaches each soul to chase its own gain by any shortcut, even at the cost of others, trading life and kin for control.

rites.name: Oreseolles
rites.text: A ward-current drawn from unmarked matter that bears no tint of any sworn hue. Those who work it say it lies outside the spectrum of the craft's wheel and answers only to raw making.

rites.name: Malaunanum
rites.text: Rivals may wager a set portion of their vitality in exchange for a chosen edge. The practice is rarely invoked, yet it lets challengers trade their own endurance for leverage.

rites.name: Tentauria
rites.text: A recurring keyword-style ability that marks a specific sense of kinship with its era's divine theme. It is tied to the tide of gods that defines its particular set of cards.

rites.name: Lirus
rites.text: A fighter that carries this trait strikes twice in a single clash of arms, once at the opening exchange alongside swift blades and again at the closing exchange alongside plain ones.

rites.name: Corontausum
rites.text: A tally of spent vitality that is gathered through a costly surrender and then held as fuel for later workings. Each stored tally can be spent to power a deliberate effect.

rites.name: Ciarnes
rites.text: A recurring toll that binds a holder to a found object. At the start of their next turn they must pay its price or surrender the object entirely.

rites.name: Ranum
rites.text: A coined naming pattern marks spells that compel a bearer to surrender one of their own beasts. Such spells are usually found among dark quick-cast and ritual scrolls.

rites.name: Mistantium
rites.text: A protective craft in which certain marks reward their bearer or punish a rival whenever goods are cast away by a foe's command. Unlike the cursed-hunger rites, these wards need no tithe of resources to awaken.

rites.name: Siantor
rites.text: A swift cursed rite that lets a practitioner draw a burst of gloom-fueled power from a single gathering of dark essence. Its strength fades over time, and its lingering influence urges followers toward shadowy craft.

rites.name: Caurnollor
rites.text: Two neighboring hues of a magic wheel that blend well together yet share a common weakness. Crafts built on them unite the strengths of both while leaving the same gap open.

rites.name: Seostanum
rites.text: A rallying call sounded as a warband charges, lending extra strength to every other fighter advancing beside the one who shouts it. It stands opposite to a solitary blessing that empowers a lone champion.

rites.name: Tialornanum
rites.text: A keyword craft that can be attached only to quick spells and rites, letting the caster pay a different price to unlock its effect.

rites.name: Cesanum
rites.text: A lawful craft by which a bound force is held in place for a time, keeping a chosen target from acting. It is practiced by a ruling council of scribes and magistrates who govern the realm's courts.

rites.name: Seollisium
rites.text: A paid alternative cost that, when chosen, also turns one of the caster's lands into a small elemental creature bearing a set number of growth tokens.

rites.name: Vollauror
rites.text: A quiet mark carried by a thing that kills whatever it strikes. Even the smallest touch from it is enough to end the life of a creature.

rites.name: Oroniallus
rites.text: A retired rule-word that once let a sorcerer hide a foe's creature beneath the earth. Later scribes replaced it with plainer commands of ruin or offering.

rites.name: Teostum
rites.text: A borrowed way of calling a fighter forth at a lower price, letting it strike at once. When the moment ends, the fighter is drawn back into its keeper's hand.

rites.name: Seontia
rites.text: A two-colored strategy of ferrying many spare resources through the sea-lanes. Its crews draw ever more supplies from each voyage, and their final push deals a crushing volley once unopposed.

rites.name: Mianum
rites.text: A practice where a bearer hides a charm beneath a plain, shielded shape for a fee. It is a stronger version of an older, weaker form of hiding.

rites.name: Oriallanum Niantor
rites.text: A small enchantment that gives back a fresh charm to its caster as it is spent, so the wielder never loses their reserve. Such small workings can be woven from any school of magic.

rites.name: Testum Lentes
rites.text: A practice in which a bearer lifts a charm from its resting place, places it into a waiting queue, and pays the required tithe so it will eventually take effect.

rites.name: Teliastus
rites.text: A craft that scales its effect by counting how many plain earth-stones of one kind a practitioner holds. Every school can wield it, though some wield it far more naturally than others.

rites.name: Tianaullus
rites.text: A deck-building craft in which a few linked components are assembled to end a contest abruptly. Its practitioners rely on swift retrieval of key pieces and on boosting resources and steady draws.

rites.name: Cantolor
rites.text: A sweeping rite that instantly unmakes every object of one chosen kind across the field. It is usually taught in pale-aligned circles, though lesser versions exist among other schools.

rites.name: Cereontus
rites.text: A common practice in which practitioners alter the strength and resilience of living beings through varied methods. Each school of craft has its own approach to it.

rites.name: Tiases
rites.text: A discipline in which a practitioner may surrender a held token to trigger a particular wondrous effect. The ritual marks the moment a keepsake is loosed into power.

rites.name: Amernisia
rites.text: A craft for binding a charm, gear, or bulwark onto another bearer or thing. It moves the bond from one holder to a new one in a single gesture.

rites.name: Oraullus
rites.text: A shared bond between two allied bearers that is awakened when one of them is roused to act. It requires both to yield their stillness so that the pair can move together.

rites.name: Telerastum
rites.text: A tide of mixed hues that rises within a casting. Spells that gather many tints of power gain greater effect the more distinct shades are poured into them.

rites.name: Corisum
rites.text: A ritual cantrip that lifts a standing token back into its keeper's palm. Its origin is unrecorded, and the term was used long before any specific crafting tool carried the name.

rites.name: Valanestium
rites.text: A gathered-labor craft that lets wheeled machines take on a living, fighting form until the turn ends. It is bound to assembled contraptions rather than to any being born of the land.

rites.name: Veoraustum
rites.text: A spell of flexible burning force, prized for its power to scorch several foes at once. Its kin are other sorcerous blasts that scale with the caster's will.

rites.name: Voneles
rites.text: A bargain-craft that lets a caster pay for a spell by offering up a standing object they already control. The offering reduces the price of the working in exchange.

rites.name: Nallosus
rites.text: A tactic where a creature sacrifices itself to gain a bonus when it enters play, used as the hallmark method of a dark, cunning clan of warriors.

rites.name: Neleonium
rites.text: A bound spell that frees a set of resting land-stones equal to its own cost value. Its casters print it as a loophole, which later proves too unstable to keep.

rites.name: Orillum
rites.text: A tactic of two linked resource-engines that gather power into a blast of surplus, then renew the chain of draws to strike with a final overwhelming surge.

rites.name: Tiarnus
rites.text: A bonding craft where a creature may draw a growth counter off itself and press it onto a newcomer that has just arrived on the field. Only beings of the same green and blue lineage can practice it.

rites.name: Valases
rites.text: A bearer of this craft can shunt harm aimed at them onto another ally under their command. The ally that takes the blow is often one sturdy enough to endure it.

rites.name: Siania Amauntastor
rites.text: Knowledge that only one party in a contest may see at a given moment. Certain rules can compel that holder to disclose what they keep concealed.

rites.name: Valisanum
rites.text: A tally of rising heat that gathers whenever a stillness falls over the ranks in a given turn. Each time the stillness holds, the bearer of the tally is scorched in return.

rites.name: Sentium
rites.text: A quickening gift that lets a newly summoned being act at once, bypassing the usual waiting period before its first deed. Beings bearing it may strike or invoke their stored rites without delay.

rites.name: Oreontia
rites.text: A rite that lets a fallen spell rise again from the burial heap by its own return price. The price demands sacrificing several other remnants from the same heap, and a risen creature may gain an added boon.

rites.name: Tausor Coronteosus
rites.text: A tactical custom where attackers strike a defender's side, so any foe who opposes the striker is weakened unless it too carries the same custom. Those who stand against it lose strength in return.

rites.name: Seontes
rites.text: A practice of casting a charm by paying its full price in raw essence rather than taking a cheaper route. Scribes and traders use the phrase to describe the plain, direct method of invoking a working.

rites.name: Maustornia
rites.text: A lingering bond that ties a creature to a rival's dwelling place, and it returns to trouble that spot whenever it is laid low.

rites.name: Oresaulium
rites.text: A colloquial phrase for a flight-bound state in which a creature can only stop foes that are also airborne. Those who soar this way are restricted to contesting only other aerial beings.

rites.name: Oraulus
rites.text: A standing trait of a creature that makes it harder for opposing beings to stand in its way. By limiting who may block it, the creature gains a better chance of striking its foe directly.

rites.name: Orirnolum
rites.text: A recurring surge of power that builds each time fallen bodies or broken fixtures are carried from the field to the burial grounds. Its strength is measured by how many such losses occur within a single turn.

rites.name: Telireosus
rites.text: A ritual technique in which a bearer sets an item aside early, paying a little now so it may be drawn on later at a reduced cost. It is a recognized method of storing up power for a future moment.

rites.name: Serarnum Telia
rites.text: A standing binding etched into certain tokens that charges any attacking creature a toll of spare energy. Over time its chief use has become outright denial, leaving foes unable to press their advance.

rites.name: Meonium
rites.text: A foretelling art that a faction of merchant-scribes can invoke from their holdings. It is tied to the ruling council of the Heron Assembly.

rites.name: Lornor
rites.text: A keyword that lets a carried implement arrive already bound to a fresh guardian. It works as the local counterpart of a similar rite found elsewhere.

rites.name: Rilia Taunium
rites.text: A lifted quality that lets a bearer rise above the reach of earthbound foes, who cannot stop it from passing overhead. It has existed since the earliest days of the realm and was among the first such gifts ever devised.

rites.name: Cianus Orelauntium
rites.text: A quiet charm that swells a creature's frame and strength when cast at the right moment. It can mimic a searing strike on an attacker or a restorative balm on a defender, rewarding those who raise verdant beasts.

rites.name: Orausontes
rites.text: A tally kept by casters of how much arcane energy they have poured into their incantations during a single turn. It marks the spent portion of their reserves, recorded so that rivals and scribes can track it.

rites.name: Nausor
rites.text: A woven energy that can be drawn from either of two sources, so each binding cost accepts one of two chosen streams. It was first recorded in a city of many guilds.

rites.name: Oreleones
rites.text: A state in which a token-like sigil is turned so its painted side shows to all onlookers. Some ledgers keep certain sigils in this open position by default, and a sigil can rest in this posture as its usual condition.

rites.name: Coreonasium
rites.text: A recurring trait where a flame-kin creature can spend its breath to briefly swell its strength for one turn. Many great wyrms carry this gift, and newer forms of it grow out of the same habit of unbound surging.

rites.name: Amistesia
rites.text: A bonding rite lets a wielder fasten a crafted gear piece onto one of their own companions by paying a set tribute. The companion that carries the gear is then called the bearer.

rites.name: Orillausor
rites.text: A dormant surge that stirs when a warrior's blood is spilled in combat. Once awakened, it drives the bearer toward ever fiercer assaults.

rites.name: Oraullum
rites.text: A bound mark of ruin that strengthens a bearer whose hand has been emptied. Sages say the less one holds back, the sharper the power grows.

rites.name: Valiarnor
rites.text: A triggered craft in which a fallen warrior bestows a lasting trait upon a foe that struck it down. The gift passes to the attacker and never fades.

rites.name: Neror
rites.text: A bonding craft in which a tool sprouts a small growth that roots itself into the wielder's grip. The growth can later bloom into a creature that fights alongside its bearer.

rites.name: Linum
rites.text: A tradition where a caster may pay a lesser price to work a spell if a rival has bled away life earlier in the same turn. It rewards the bold who strike first.

rites.name: Orausanum
rites.text: A principle where a single arcane effect strikes every participant in the same manner. Those who grasp its balance gain an edge in both preparation and play.

rites.name: Neornus
rites.text: A tactic in which a practitioner unmakes the ground-bearing sigils of a rival, or a relic that does so. Its aim is to strip the opponent of the places their power is drawn from.

rites.name: Salosor
rites.text: A flexible midrange strategy that answers each rival approach with situational tools it can seek out. Its cunning rests on a famous mistake: a misspelled forum thread gave it a lasting name.

rites.name: Resus
rites.text: A craft by which a ground is reshaped so that it yields a different kind of resource. Practitioners of the cold arts mostly use it to reach resources they could not otherwise gather in crowded realms.

rites.name: Tontanus
rites.text: A quickness that a traveler may carry within themselves, tied to the moment a journey's engines are first roused. It is a gift of motion that shapes how swiftly one moves through the world.

rites.name: Corintalium
rites.text: A practice in which a bearer draws one or more cards, then discards an equal number. The discards almost always go to the grave pile.

rites.name: Rollaurium
rites.text: A swift, lean strategy in which a band of cheap, fast creatures tries to overwhelm a rival before the battle can stall. Its wielders win quickly or not at all, and a frost-sealed relic forces foes to hurry alongside them.

rites.name: Serantium Valelosium
rites.text: A quiet trait carried by certain beings that lets them slip past defenders and makes them impossible to stop by ordinary guards. Such beings can only be opposed by others who share the same stealthy nature.

rites.name: Seriallium
rites.text: A craft that lets a practitioner seize command of an opponent's bound thing, either keeping it for good or borrowing it for a single turn. Most often it claims beasts and guardians.

rites.name: Ninum
rites.text: A fast, all-in tactic where a red-aligned crew deploys small, cheap fighters each turn to drain an opponent's life. Survivors are finished with burning spells, and ruining the rival's resources keeps them from answering.

rites.name: Valeosinia
rites.text: A practice where a keeper sends the topmost tokens of a sealed reserve down into a pit of spent things. The reserve shrinks while the pit grows heavier with discarded lore.

rites.name: Valeostum
rites.text: A bound creature is unable to strike or guard while its foe keeps a steady, direct sight upon it. The hold lasts only as long as the gaze does.

rites.name: Tiasternium
rites.text: A bearer glances at a set number of uppermost slips from a hidden archive, then sends them below or returns them above in any sequence they choose. It appears on scrolls, charms, relics, and banners across many workshops.

rites.name: Telauntirus
rites.text: A recurring knack that stirs a small effect whenever a practitioner casts or duplicates a quick charm or a swift incantation. It is taught in scholarly halls where young casters learn to channel their spellwork.

rites.name: Lonia Ceriasanum
rites.text: A keyword power that makes a spell produce a duplicate of itself for every spell cast earlier in the same turn. It can grow overwhelmingly strong when many cheap spells are cast together.

rites.name: Valerium
rites.text: A reckless single-hued strategy that floods the field with cheap, aggressive shadow creatures, accepting heavy costs to finish the contest before those costs bite. It leans on forced discard and clearing answers to keep rivals from disrupting the charge.

rites.name: Oreolarnes
rites.text: A dark craft where a creature that wounds another and sees it perish grows stronger. Its wielders find foes often avoid their strikes or swarm them, so the growth rarely comes.

rites.name: Montausum
rites.text: A process that turns a living creature into a machine-like being of a cold metal faction. The transformation rewrites flesh into the shape of that faction's engineered servants.

rites.name: Viastinia
rites.text: A coined ward that keeps a creature or person from being chosen as the aim of any charm or enchantment. It is a quiet guard that blocks targeted magic before it can land.

rites.name: Lianor
rites.text: A tutoring-craft that exists only in spells of quick casting and sudden effect. It is closely tied to the act of gaining instruction in the middle of a fight.

rites.name: Lasteonia
rites.text: A practitioner may pay an extra price when casting a charm to unlock a second, added effect. The surplus cost is optional and grants a bonus outcome.

rites.name: Tialum
rites.text: A dormant stillness that can settle over beings and hold them frozen in place. It works as a tally that marks how long the stillness lingers.

rites.name: Corilanum
rites.text: When a certain bound guardian falls, its keeper may draw back from the burial pits a lesser ally whose cost does not exceed a set measure. Most of these guardians carry a cost exactly one higher than that measure.

rites.name: Lilauntia
rites.text: A craft of binding foes with lasting jinxes that bar them from acting. It is practiced by dark-aligned hands and paired with other sorcerous schemes that stall rivals.

rites.name: Sereloria Valiastes
rites.text: A keyword ability that lets certain bearers grow stronger by gathering enough accumulated charge. It is carried mainly by a particular class of rising creatures.

rites.name: Telonus Cilesanum
rites.text: A ritual binding that lets swift incantations and quick rites take on a shifting mode. The practice gives such workings a changeable manner each time they are cast.

rites.name: Taullus
rites.text: A tradition of keeping charged tokens that a bearer may spend to awaken a single chosen art each turn, and only during the bearer's own deliberate moments. The tokens belong to the person carrying them, not to the object they were struck upon.

rites.name: Nillia
rites.text: A bonded rider-craft that only takes hold on beasts of burden and mounts. It is an ability that can be lent to the creatures bearing that kind of trait.

rites.name: Naurilium
rites.text: A bound working of magic that a caster releases from the hand by drawing on ritual and learned lore. Before it takes effect, it waits as a pending force that others may answer.

rites.name: Nonum Seorialium
rites.text: A tolling craft in which an enchantment blocks a rival's action until they surrender a measure of their reserved power. Most often bound to standing wards and sometimes cast once as a sudden toll.

rites.name: Meosor
rites.text: A ritual that draws a chosen treasure from a keeper's archive of sealed scrolls. The reader calls upon the archive to bring forth a single named tome.

rites.name: Orolum
rites.text: A coined tactic lets a warrior borrow an enemy beast for one turn, rousing it to sudden speed. Clans favor it for sacrificing stolen creatures to gain rewards.

rites.name: Reranum
rites.text: A protective veil clings to a bearer, so that a binding charm is consumed in its place when the bearer would fall. If the bearer is a fighter, its wounds are wiped away, much like a restoring healing ritual.

rites.name: Orastes
rites.text: A bearer is open to strikes aimed straight at it, as though it were a fortress under siege. Foes may choose to challenge it directly, bypassing its allies entirely.

rites.name: Oranium
rites.text: A tally-mark that gathers slowly on a bearer, carrying a drawback when only one is held and a reward when three gather. Reaching four or more wipes the count clean.

rites.name: Vastia Leosontus
rites.text: A ritual craft in which a caster gathers all held and discarded tokens back into the deck, then draws a fresh opening set. It belongs to the wider family of cycling workings.

rites.name: Sauntolum
rites.text: A stacked tactic of drawing and holding onto many resources until one of a few narrow finishing conditions becomes available. Its practitioners rely on quick bursts of fuel and countermagic to protect their hoard.

rites.name: Rasum
rites.text: A combat gift that lets a warrior drive its strikes past any defender as though no foe stood in the way. It belongs chiefly to the verdant clans and was once called by a rougher nickname.

rites.name: Valastum
rites.text: A shorthand chant that names the five hues of arcane power, one of each color used to fuel spells. Practitioners recite it as a mnemonic when gathering their energies.

rites.name: Orausteorum
rites.text: A tally mark drawn for each joined rebel band. Every creature a leader commands stands a little stronger for each mark carried.

rites.name: Serantium
rites.text: A quiet inherited trait that lets a bearer's touch pass harmlessly over the dead. It appears only in a single rare trick known as a last stand.

rites.name: Costanes
rites.text: A craft by which a wounding force spawns a matching number of small, identical echoes for its bearer. Each echo takes the same form and hue as the force that woke it.

rites.name: Teorentus
rites.text: A wayfarer's craft that lets one cross between separate worlds of reality. It is employed only in one unofficial trading card, linked to a single bearer who wears a dimmed, reversed sun.

rites.name: Naurnium
rites.text: A glowing mark that clings to a thing and, once that thing is broken and cast away, flares to strike a rival for two points of harm. It can guard a treasure or ambush a foe.

rites.name: Rillia
rites.text: A bargain-spell whose strength the caster chooses at the moment of casting, paid in a flexible resource. Some incantations accept only one kind of essence for this open share.

rites.name: Teleonentor
rites.text: A proposed action in which a card is struck twice in quick succession. It has been imagined by designers but never put into play, and would need its own marker to signal it.

rites.name: Tiasolia
rites.text: A reckless rush of power that a creature can be cast with at a steep alternative price. It lets the bearer strike hard and fast, then vanish after the blow lands.

rites.name: Merium
rites.text: A joining craft that fuses two separate tokens into one unified form upon the field. It works mainly through a bond where a base and an attachment merge into a single creature, and certain wardens can fuse ordinary beings in the same way.

rites.name: Tellum
rites.text: A ritual gesture that turns a two-sided token over to reveal its reverse form. It works exactly like the older turning rite known as the Mirror Turn.

rites.name: Valoniasum
rites.text: A shared-effort craft in which companions pitch in part of the cost when someone casts a spell. The helpers cover only the general portion of that cost, leaving the caster's specific requirements to them alone.

rites.name: Mintiarnum
rites.text: A quiet craft in which a caster lets remembered relics from the discard heap stand in for part of an incantation's cost. It works only while the incantation hangs unresolved in the air.

rites.name: Moniallanum
rites.text: A tactical trick in which a creature that strikes an enemy also lets its wielder draw a fresh card. It is a sabotage-style skill that belongs mostly to one mental discipline and partly to another.

rites.name: Amiallia
rites.text: A tactic where a spell may be empowered by sacrificing a creature the caster controls. Choosing this extra cost lets the spell strike harder.

rites.name: Amonium
rites.text: A triggered quality that marks certain colorless hulking beings, letting them force an opponent to surrender pieces of their standing forces whenever those beings strike.

rites.name: Mirnes
rites.text: A grinding strategy of control that burdens rivals by levying costs on their every move. Its practitioners rely on a dazzling sequence of clever maneuvers, often driven by a fast, flickering device.

rites.name: Nauntaror
rites.text: A hidden scheming art that shapes the outcome of a conflict in secret. It is practiced by a clandestine guild of city schemers as their signature method of working in the shadows.

rites.name: Oreorus
rites.text: A shifting trait that marks certain shapeshifting beings, letting them take on every form of kind. Only those born to change carry it.

rites.name: Liarus
rites.text: A forbidden ritual that siphons the inner flame of mighty wielders to raise one caster toward divinity. Its origin is lost, and seekers of old lore recognize it as ancient, primal sorcery.

rites.name: Rinollum
rites.text: A tally that holds back an effect until a later round begins. Each tally is counted down at the start of that round before the held effect takes hold.

rites.name: Carnonium
rites.text: A combat craft in which fallen warriors left in the dead-pile become a reserve that empowers the living later. Its makers chose not to bind it with a formal title.

rites.name: Nauntus
rites.text: Effects that recolor a spell or lasting object, usually only until the turn ends. Azure workers recolor other things, verdant ones recolor themselves, and pale and dark ones can make things take their own hue.

rites.name: Ralestor
rites.text: A practice of setting a card onto the field turned face down, hidden from view. It is a stronger version of an older method of laying out a card in concealment.

rites.name: Tosenus
rites.text: A tally of tainted marks that gathers on a single bearer of ruin. Only one particular wandering sorcerer is able to set these marks and count them.

rites.name: Ceornus
rites.text: A practice that lets a bearer surrender a bound token as part of a payment. Once the exchange is completed, the bearer takes a fresh draw from the supply.

rites.name: Niallines
rites.text: A standing gift that lets a creature consume its foes upon arrival. Each time such a creature enters play, it may swallow a number of rival creatures and grow stronger for every one it takes in.

rites.name: Vostum
rites.text: A practitioner lifts a bound token from its resting place, places it upon a waiting stack, and settles its price so the working can later unfold. Patience before the working is considered wise.

rites.name: Riarnes
rites.text: A grim sigil of an unseen mechanism that lets a creature slip past foes whose strength is no greater than two. It is most readily drawn from the verdant lineage.

rites.name: Corentes
rites.text: A tactical maneuver formally introduced for a solitary ruler, allowing an effect to be performed twice in a single action. It is recorded in the ledgers of that realm's courts.

rites.name: Maurnus
rites.text: A recurring craft in which a sparked effect chains onward, reaching for further effects each time it is set off. It was first recorded within a later age of the realm.

rites.name: Amenum
rites.text: A dormant rite that delays a chronicle's unfolding until the day's final quiet moment. It was first sketched on a trial scroll tested among a small circle of archivists.

rites.name: Telestus
rites.text: A dormant rule of contagion that alters a bearer's nature once a rival has been stricken by three or more lingering toxins. It awakens only when the afflicted reach that threshold.

rites.name: Sanintum
rites.text: A practitioner calls forth new tokens of cards that were never part of their collection. Once summoned, these created cards behave like ordinary ones for the rest of the contest.

rites.name: Sintium Maurnum
rites.text: A quiet rule under which a marked card is treated as bearing no abilities at all. It appears only on a single trial card made for testing.

rites.name: Corelontium
rites.text: A learned practice in which a wanderer uncovers a hidden card from a cavern of lost lore. The found card may then be cast or placed in the hand.

rites.name: Naulises
rites.text: A rule describes a creature that makes a lone assault without any companions beside it. It is commonly used as a drawback, and the opposite condition appears rarely.

rites.name: Saullorium
rites.text: A rarely invoked tactical craft in which a creature's sturdiness is turned into striking force. Some wardens of several guilds also learn to let their guardians strike in battle.

rites.name: Veoraunor
rites.text: A rare rule that erases every copy of one chosen card from the whole contest, from the field, the discard piles, the hands, the decks, and the reserve stacks. The erasure holds until the contest is finished.

rites.name: Amentires
rites.text: A former practice where a group of linked effects waits to take hold until every one of them has finished. This prevents an opponent from answering a boost by striking the target before it grows.

rites.name: Serolaurum
rites.text: A tactic that lets a single casting bring forth a pair of creatures at once. It exists only within a digital arena of play.

rites.name: Ceolenor
rites.text: A craft that makes one thing into a duplicate of another. When aimed at a living being it is called a shaping of twins. The duplicate takes only the original's fixed traits, ignoring any passing alterations.

rites.name: Nosum
rites.text: A stirring art that a being may call upon whenever it advances on an opponent and no defender steps in to stop it. Its power then wakes and takes effect.

rites.name: Siasor
rites.text: A clever scheme where a gifted mind hands a cursed boon to a rival, who must bleed away their strength paying its toll until they collapse. Allied wardens and forbidden bargains guard the plan.

rites.name: Tesum
rites.text: A reckless two-color scheme that empties its own hand, fills the burial pile with looted draws, and then swings with returned creatures. Each turn it chases a sudden lethal strike.

rites.name: Casum Corontianor
rites.text: A nimble manner of moving that lets certain agile warriors slip past defenses by paying an alternate price. Only a few swift fighters of the shadowy guild are trained in it.

rites.name: Rasirnum
rites.text: A lasting quality that keeps a bound object from being broken or unmade by any rule or force. It stays present no matter what the realm's laws or spells attempt against it.

rites.name: Loriantia
rites.text: A green combo craft that gathers lands to build a massive engine of mana, then casts a spell that brings a powerful team of creatures into play at once. Its strength lies in forcing that spell past layers of countermagic.

rites.name: Corenantia
rites.text: A practiced act of looking closely into a matter to uncover what lies hidden. It was first adopted in one age of study and later carried into another, and it eventually took root and grew into common use.

rites.name: Cornia Oraullenium
rites.text: A lingering sense that doom is drawing near settles over whoever feels it. It conveys the quiet dread of knowing a reckoning is coming.

rites.name: Valontialum
rites.text: A nickname for briefly banishing a thing from play and then restoring it to its place on the field. Some crafters call the same trick a blink, though a true blink returns a creature to its owner's hand instead.

rites.name: Valantia
rites.text: A marker that gets placed on exiled cards, letting its owner cast them later. It belongs to a partner ability that unlocks these hidden cards.

rites.name: Seresum
rites.text: A quiet suspension that freezes the field in place while a pending charm waits to resolve. Nothing on the battlefield may be shifted or relocated until that charm has finished its work.

rites.name: Leorenum
rites.text: A bargain that lets a summoner pay a lesser price to call forth a being, but the being is destroyed the moment it arrives. The summoned one vanishes as soon as it steps into the world.

rites.name: Caustia
rites.text: A bargaining craft in which a caster surrenders a kindred presence back to their palm in return for a cheaper invocation or a stronger bearing. Its rites were once gathered into a single sweeping rift of the realm.

rites.name: Nausum
rites.text: A bond ability on certain creatures that lets their controller empower another creature alongside them. It is a newer variant of an older shared-strength custom.

rites.name: Mastum Coreostones
rites.text: A layered control craft that hides behind many counters and draws on a binding rite to summon either a helping creature or a towering finisher. Recovered helpers are returned to the stock so the rite can call them again.

rites.name: Oreostiania
rites.text: A looping tactic where a sorcerous mind-caster empties an entire archive into its spent pile, then calls back a grim giant to swing for victory. It demands spells of many colors and rarely wins quickly.

rites.name: Terum
rites.text: An old class of swift cast that once rushed ahead of every other pending action. Its rules were revised away, and their echo lives on in a later mechanic that stops responses.

rites.name: Orirum
rites.text: A blue-only control strategy that uses cheap spells to flood its pool with mana, then unleashes a huge surge to overwhelm an opponent. It relies on defensive countermagic and steady card drawing.

rites.name: Renistia
rites.text: A dreadful unsettling quality that clings to enchantments and the chambers of a haunted dwelling, marking them as strange and uncanny.

rites.name: Ceosellus
rites.text: A tournament plan blending three colors of control with sturdy hard-to-kill threats. It answers both creature swarms and rival control decks, and surprises opponents at a major gathering.

rites.name: Sianum
rites.text: A compelling rite that drives a creature to charge into battle against a rival other than its summoner. It was devised for gatherings of many contenders.

rites.name: Oreollium
rites.text: A paired allegiance shared between two champions of a tournament style called Commander. It lets each partner in the bond lend the other a particular shared binding, and it was introduced as an earlier version of an older pairing rule.

rites.name: Meontes
rites.text: A slow, grinding strategy that sacrifices its own territory-bearing sites to flood its pool with power, then wipes the battlefield clean. It finishes with a massive creature fed by the discarded ground beneath.

rites.name: Mernes
rites.text: A practice in which a sealed vessel is filled with growth counters, each one a small increase in strength. The vessel's count is set by the number named when the practice is called upon.

rites.name: Tosteosanum
rites.text: A practice closely resembling foresight, except that it reaches into a rival's store of coming fortunes instead of one's own. The act of sealing another's destiny sets it apart from ordinary sight.

rites.name: Orauronanum
rites.text: A ritual technique that lets a caster call a spent incantation back from the discard pile by sacrificing another card from hand. The recalled spell is banished once its effect resolves.

rites.name: Resteoranum
rites.text: A tactic of two hands that builds steady advantage over long stretches before ending with a towering beast. Its cards shift over time while the plan itself stays the same.

rites.name: Corasium
rites.text: A tournament strategy where a large creature is cast, every land is wiped away, and the heavy threat then batters an opponent who is short on mana.

rites.name: Teliarum
rites.text: A looping engine built from cheap egg-artifacts that keeps returning a single recurring spell to the table. It draws out endless mana until the opponent is finished off by repeated bombs or a stolen mind-blast.

rites.name: Lastia Maliarnum
rites.text: A practice where a caster may cast spells drawn from the top of a deck of fate-cards, guided by a foresight that lets them glimpse what lies ahead.

rites.name: Vosia Cintum
rites.text: A layered strategy of repeated shifting that sends chosen creatures out of a clash and back again. Early and late uses of a great winged beast help it draw resources and close out the contest.

rites.name: Ceollaunes
rites.text: A keyword ability that marks an additional cost attached to a card's effect. The cost must be paid as an extra condition before the effect can be used.

rites.name: Neontor
rites.text: A rule that lets a spell with several optional effects carry an extra cost, so the caster may choose more than one of its options. It is found only on certain spells that offer a menu of choices.

rites.name: Rialanum Vaulus
rites.text: A tactical engine of layered tricks that a crafty sorcerer assembles to draw extra cards and bind foes. Its cheap utility pieces disrupt rivals' schemes, and a clever wish-spell fetches hidden answers from a reserve pile.

rites.name: Naustanum
rites.text: A tactic where a looping device spawns winged copies of tiny creatures by spending small resources. Each spent resource yields another flyer and a little vitality, growing into a swarm that becomes hard to wear down.

rites.name: Nialenor
rites.text: A swift engine of stacked cheap spells that unleashes a flood of colossal monsters at once. The gathered giants tear through the field and usually finish a rival within a couple of rounds.

rites.name: Mastosor
rites.text: A forced halt that cuts short the current cycle of play, sometimes leaving a lingering doom for the next round. Only one rare decree can close a whole stage of the cycle.

rites.name: Vorentor
rites.text: A protective magical shield encloses an entire world, erected by a single caster to keep outside wielders of planar power from harming the land and its people.

rites.name: Lontelia
rites.text: A marked power that certain legendary beings carry, awakening when they are placed in play from the command zone. It rewards a commander's presence by granting its bearer a lasting, empowered effect.

rites.name: Vausteontor
rites.text: A practice of binding a living thing so its keeper cannot command it, without slaying it. Two common methods are a calming enchantment that stops it from fighting and a banishing sigil that holds it away while the sigil endures.

rites.name: Rases
rites.text: A shared pooling practice where several participants each contribute any amount of their energy to one token, and the combined total determines a single effect that favors every contributor equally.

rites.name: Oriantus
rites.text: A trait that activates when a creature bearing it strikes a rival in battle. The struck rival must surrender the topmost card from their stack of reserves into exile.

rites.name: Sollor
rites.text: A rule that lets a caster draw a spell from the discard heap by paying a different price. The card is banished once the spell resolves, and a sibling rule serves the same purpose for standing objects.

rites.name: Telolestus
rites.text: A withering craft that binds a made thing to a limited span of rounds, after which it dissolves from the field. It was later replaced by a simpler dissolving rite, since its workings confused many practitioners.

rites.name: Naulum
rites.text: A practiced seer may reveal a glimpsed card during a divining, and then cast it by paying a separate hidden price. The craft first surfaced in a trial sheet shown at a gathering of collectors.

rites.name: Teontium
rites.text: A bond that a wandering caster holds to their sworn ally, tracked by marks. It is not their life force, but harm wearing it down leaves the caster unwilling to aid and eventually drives them off.

rites.name: Serantorium
rites.text: A binding craft that forces an opposing bearer to meet certain attackers in battle. Any such attacker compels the defender to answer it, narrowing their choices when they guard.

rites.name: Vireonor
rites.text: A bound ward that makes a creature impossible to stop in combat whenever its opponent holds at least one land of a matching kind. It has since been retired from the rules.

rites.name: Coreonium Teleolia
rites.text: A standing permission that lets a leader's company carry extra kinds of cards beyond the usual color limits. It is marked by a special word that signals the exception.

rites.name: Lianus
rites.text: A dual-tapping archetype where lands that yield any color support a broad control strategy. The craft gathers many potent spells into one design and wins through a single forceful finisher.

rites.name: Valinum
rites.text: A tactic of steady, controlling play built around a single-colored dark strategy. It takes its name from an older contagion-themed card that a newer, similar card later came to replace.

rites.name: Oriantus Coresalium
rites.text: A tactic where a lone mind channels a stone engine's surge into endless energy, drawing fresh resources while shielding its wielder from harm until a single decisive strike ends the contest.

rites.name: Valolisanum
rites.text: A swift mechanic lets a creature strike the very turn it arrives, yet its bearer must settle a heavy debt on the next turn or be undone. Later bargains of borrowed time echo this gamble.

rites.name: Milontum
rites.text: A chained ritual where a card-drawing rite is followed by a lethal drain, fueled by a stream of cheap mana sources. Hand disruption shields the sequence from interference by rivals.

rites.name: Tenaulus
rites.text: A tally marker that is added through repeated payments. When a creature attacks, it lets the holder recast copies of cards set aside in exile.

rites.name: Molanum
rites.text: A binding rule that keeps a newly called creature inert until its keeper has held it through a full cycle of their own turn. Those who break the rule find their summoned beast cannot strike or stir.

rites.name: Amaunum
rites.text: A triggered effect that fires when a standing object is removed from play, judged by the state of the world just before its removal. An object that vanishes because its keeper departs the match still counts, unless it is temporarily hidden away.

rites.name: Teliantum
rites.text: A cunning card-based strategy in which a cluster of enchanting charms draws in more charms and bearers of magic. Lasting wards and recycled spells keep rivals at bay while tokens finish the match.

rites.name: Riales
rites.text: A tactic in which a practitioner deliberately sacrifices their own vitality to empower a dark, looming curse. It spread from a newer arena into an older, established one.

rites.name: Corolium Vinastum
rites.text: A quiet rite where a caster reaches into a sealed archive and the archive itself chooses a fitting relic, which then passes straight into the caster's grasp.

rites.name: Maunus
rites.text: A single-hued fiery craft in which a practitioner builds up a rising chain of quick spells and then unleashes them all at once for a decisive finishing blow. Several rival schools teach slightly different versions of the same method.

rites.name: Coreollarum
rites.text: A ritual call that rouses the swift machines of the land to life. It is bound to the art of speed.

rites.name: Ciseontus
rites.text: A binding quality that lets a force mend its bearer whenever it strikes. Each wound it inflicts returns an equal measure of vitality to whoever wielded it.

rites.name: Aminanum
rites.text: A marked designation can be placed on a being, making it draw attacks from others. The mark encourages hostile action toward the bearer.

rites.name: Tarium
rites.text: A theoretical bond that splits a double-faced token into two halves, each carrying one side of an incantation. Only by pairing a left half with a right half from separate tokens can the full working be unleashed.

rites.name: Veolinor
rites.text: Certain dark-hued beings grow stronger when they stand alone among their owner's creatures. Their solitude is the opposite of a bonded pairing, and the idea rarely returns.

rites.name: Teleoranum
rites.text: A mechanical rule that a creature or thing may be given an amount of power tied to a light-like charge. The rule proved disliked when first introduced and was later reworked into a different rule with a similar purpose.

rites.name: Teleolus
rites.text: A tactical strategy where a looping engine of sacrifice and selection draws cards repeatedly and fetches specialized creatures to answer any threat. Its reliance on one dominant engine later brought the entire approach to ruin by decree.

rites.name: Ceornium Amiraullus
rites.text: A practice in which a bearer lends strength to nearby allies by placing small growth markers upon their forms. The markers stay until the bearer's chosen companions grow stronger together.

rites.name: Neornirus
rites.text: A discounted way to cast a spell, granted when another spell is already in play alongside it. Casters pay less for it as a reward for linking the two.

rites.name: Orellaurium
rites.text: A three-colored tactic that fires searing bursts to clear enemy guardians, draws extra resources through clever trades, and finishes with winged champions striking hard.

rites.name: Nestes
rites.text: A grave-tending craft in which a fallen body's remnants are reclaimed to bolster a living ally. The practice works like a second chance drawn from the dead, sending a spent thing back into use with added vigor.

rites.name: Tolliror
rites.text: A patient strategy built from many single-copy cards that gather advantage and answer threats before a final large threat closes the contest. It is notoriously demanding, and skilled handling is said to make every match winnable.

rites.name: Sasoria
rites.text: A patient build that holds back early pressure while drawing many cards, then assembles a towering engine of linked stones that leaves its holder with a crushing advantage.

rites.name: Tauntia
rites.text: A tide-driven craft in which a swarm of quick cast spells floods a rival's sources, reshuffling and draining the field until the opponent's library is emptied and the caster prevails.

rites.name: Valanus Coreostasum
rites.text: A marked sign that a rite gains new effects, or may only be invoked, once a creature has perished earlier in the same turn. It alters how a spell behaves after a death.

rites.name: Niallanum
rites.text: A tactic that exploits a fuel-gathering rule to power up cheap, sturdy attackers quickly. Its wielders also hold back opposing magic and burn foes directly to win fast.

rites.name: Orilum
rites.text: A deck-based craft that wins by emptying an opponent's library through layered card draws and rapid cycling. It relies on a flood of spells that thin the draw pile until it runs dry.

rites.name: Sereolor
rites.text: A dark ritual that strips every copy of a chosen object from a rival's possession, banishing it from their hand, reserves, and resting place. Scholars liken it to a mind being hollowed out.

rites.name: Rantum
rites.text: A patient strategy that floods the holder's hand by drawing extra cards, then returns threats to the opponent's hand and uses a carved owl figure to chip away at their life. Heavy control tools keep the foe's land locked and their spells countered.

rites.name: Causeolum
rites.text: A fast, aggressive craft where a lone shapeshifting tinkerer rushes to transform into a swift winged form early on. Quick burning strikes and sudden counters aim to finish rivals before they can respond.

rites.name: Rentarnia
rites.text: A bound craft in which a standing relic is shifted by its keeper's will, altering the tally sealed upon its vessel. Each shift is a deliberate action that changes that tally.

rites.name: Vialenus
rites.text: A loosely named practice where cards from one realm trigger extra effects whenever a spirit or ritual spell is cast. Some of these effects gather small charged tokens that accumulate over play.

rites.name: Valorianus
rites.text: A tactic where a swift attacking ghost-knight and a pair of enchanted blades press the foe early. Counterspells and removal shield the strategy while cheap, powerful creatures keep the pressure on.

rites.name: Oreornianus
rites.text: A tactic where a dying guardian binds the rival for a turn, and a deep-searching engine lets the user chain such guardians to leave the opponent hopelessly behind.

rites.name: Coreostium
rites.text: A digital-only craft that lets a legendary being take on a new hue and fresh powers. It works much like picking a past life to shape a hero's story.

rites.name: Telalor
rites.text: A craft of linking many tokens of power so each one strengthens its neighbors. Clusters built this way outperform stronger pieces that work against one another.

rites.name: Nornes
rites.text: A patient tactic that freezes a contest by locking the opposing side in place. Its users slip the lock aside briefly to refresh their own resources, then wait for the foe to run dry.

rites.name: Vauliarnus
rites.text: A method by which a two-sided token is flipped over to reveal its opposite face. The visible side changes as a result of this turning.

rites.name: Viarium Seriantum
rites.text: A lingering corruption that lets a creature carry several blight marks at once. It replaces an older form of the same curse and reflects the warped nature of its origin.

rites.name: Naustornes
rites.text: A quiet rite that buries an object beneath the owner's deck, or mixes it back among the rest. The sunken thing is hidden from easy reach, though a later shuffle or a sage's call may bring it back up.

rites.name: Lentisus
rites.text: A rule where a creature that is blocked turns the blocker's strength against it. It works like a charge through the defenders that stand in the way.

rites.name: Caraulor
rites.text: A craft that rewrites the inscribed words on a bearer's sigil, scroll, or title plate. Practitioners call such workings word-changers or quiet hacks.

rites.name: Sornistia
rites.text: A rule that lets an attacker push past the blocker in battle. When the strike lands, damage that would be absorbed by the defending shield can instead spill over to the target behind it.

rites.name: Nilia
rites.text: A rule that stops a creature from being stopped by defenders. Its effect is written plainly on the card, marking the creature as impossible to intercept.

rites.name: Visor
rites.text: A bound rule-force that acts on its own whenever a specified occurrence unfolds, or whenever a set of standing conditions becomes true. Some such forces stir only while the conditions hold, never needing a single moment of trigger.

rites.name: Coriasum
rites.text: A binding craft that caps how many rounds a conjured thing may linger in the world before it dissolves. It runs on the passing of time as a finite resource, and it works as the reverse of a delayed-summoning rite.

rites.name: Coreostirum
rites.text: A craft that alters a bearer's form into a new shade and kind, setting its strength and endurance to fixed values. It is commonly practiced through a particular school of mystic study.

rites.name: Siarnia
rites.text: A rare binding craft that lets a bearer exchange a standing creature-form for another from their own hidden reserve. Only one artifact is known to carry it, and its makers rarely seek to repeat it.

rites.name: Silannae
rites.text: Silannae is a bound spirit of tidal memory, kept sleeping beneath the glass floors of the Orierlae archives since the third age. It can be woken only by a chorus of willing voices, and when it stirs it can quiet a sea's worth of rage into obedience.

rites.name: Nuemallora
rites.text: Nuemallora is a concept of layered binding-sigils that a caster inscribes across their own spellwork, letting a single incantation borrow the stored resonance of older rites. Its practitioners treat it as a discipline of restraint, since each borrowed layer deepens the cost paid in memory and breath.

rites.name: Nuilaerleth
rites.text: Nuilaerleth is an arcane discipline in Orierlae's sixth era, practiced by scholars who bind their own breath into sigils that answer to ley-currents. Its adepts are prized for turning modest personal reserves into sudden, focused detonations that can crack a fortress wall.

rites.name: Alaamiel
rites.text: Alaamiel is a binding-discipline of the Arcane realm in Orierlae, practiced in the third age of the E6 era by scholars who inscribe lattices of silence into their own vocal cords. Its adepts can channel sealed rites that briefly hold the weight of a dying star's gravity inside a ring of runes. The discipline is restricted to those who have already sworn a formal oath to a pact or a spellcasting order.

rites.name: Elineirleth
rites.text: Elineirleth is a ceremonial rite of the Orierlae Arcane Choirs, performed by those who have mastered a sung tradition of binding. Its practitioners draw the slow decay of living growth into their voices, releasing it as a single resonant surge when the choir reaches its final chord.

rites.name: Ilyemora
rites.text: Ilyemora is a bound-song of the Orierlae arcane tradition, a ritual pattern that lets a caster channel stored ley-resonance into layered tones. Its practitioners are sworn to the old choir-halls of the E6 age, where it is taught only after years of silent study.

rites.name: Miinnuarora
rites.text: Miinnuarora is a crystalline arcane discipline from the Orierlae age of E6, practiced by scholars who channel auroral light through prisms of frozen memory. Its adepts can briefly sear a city's skyline into glowing afterimages or hold a storm of radiance in a single lantern.

rites.name: Sileimenys
rites.text: Sileimenys is a mnemonic discipline of the Arcane realm in the third age of Orierlae, in which a caster binds a sealed ledger of vows to their own breath. Practitioners who master it can unmake a bound oath and release the stored force of broken promises as a single concussive burst.

rites.name: Sileimora
rites.text: Sileimora is a silent tide of cold lamplight that drifts through the sunken libraries of Orierlae, quietly unbinding any working spell it touches. Scholars of the drowned archives believe it was once the memory of a dying star-choir, and its currents still steer those who listen too closely.

rites.name: Ilyinys
rites.text: Ilyinys is a bonded resonance of the Arcane realm in the Orierlae omniverse, a silver lattice of sung glyphs that a caster weaves into their spellwork during the sixth era. It answers only to those who have already learned to shape magic, amplifying their workings by drawing on the hum of their own crystal-bound oath.

rites.name: Orienareth
rites.text: Orienareth is a discipline of woven resonance taught in the drowned cloisters of Orierlae, where practitioners bind their own heartbeat to tidal sigils. It is classed as a concept rather than a physical body, shaping how spellcasters draw force from the ocean's rhythm.

rites.name: Miirla
rites.text: Miirla is a bound charm of the Orierlae concept-realm, a silver filigree disc that lets its holder call one of three old working-words into being: a binding that stills a mind, a single clipped command, or a ward that unravels a spell mid-breath. It was carved in the third age of the Kessane hill-schools and remains a favored tool of their wardens.

rites.name: Nuaniorlora
rites.text: Nuaniorlora is a silvered signet ring carried by the lawkeepers of the Orierlae archive-cities, engraved with a sealed scroll and a bronze key. Wearers can bind a foe in a net of shimmering verbal glyphs, a snare that tightens with each recited clause of the oath.

rites.name: Ryileth
rites.text: Ryileth is a silver-threaded arcane charm woven during the sixth age of Orierlae, a relic that grants its bearer borrowed swiftness or a shield of resolve. Its wearers are said to hear the hum of distant ley currents whenever it wakes.

rites.name: Miemuareth
rites.text: Miemuareth is a silver signet of the Orierlae arcane cartographers, engraved with a sunrise over a broken crown, that lends its bearer a surge of unbending resolve. Its grandest recorded use kindled a sealed, starless vault and lit the cold dark for a generation of dreamers.

rites.name: Orierioniel
rites.text: Orierioniel is a glimmering charm of woven silver filament that hums when a bearer's breath matches its rhythm, allowing a sudden shift across a short distance or a drowsy calm to settle over a room. Its wearers are forbidden from using it twice in one dawn, a custom enforced by the Lantern Wardens of Orierlae.

rites.name: Ilyirlys
rites.text: Ilyirlys is a band of tarnished silver worn by the shadow-scribes of the Veilmoot, carved with a closed eye wreathed in ink-black thorns. Its wearer may slip a borrowed face over their own for as long as the ring holds its breath, though each borrowed face leaves a faint ache in the bone. Old scribes say the ring once concealed an entire ferry crossing from the tide-gods, a feat that still shapes the river's name.

rites.name: Silarora
rites.text: Silarora is a bound lattice-charm of the Arcane realm in the Orierlae omniverse, worn as a pendant of cooled glass that hums when its three seals are struck. Its wielders in the third age use it to unmake enchantments, to draw a temporary reserve of vitality, or to release a choking fog of sulfur and rot. Its power is modest but reliable, and the old archives record it as a favored tool of field mages.

rites.name: Venamys
rites.text: Venamys is a concept of living root-sigils woven into the sap-cords of the Orierlae arcane courts, drawn upon by those who command tangling growth. In its third age, Venamys is passed among favored sworn ones as a token of trust, letting the bearer knot the earth itself into snaring vines.

rites.name: Miirlora
rites.text: Miirlora is a silver-threaded charm of the Arcane era, worn by wandering sigil-singers of Orierlae to answer a sudden need for courage or a thunderous shove. Its bearers say it hums faintly when a storm is near, as though the sky itself recognizes its making.

rites.name: Silennys
rites.text: Silennys is a dormant arcane concept in the Orierlae omniverse, a ring that a sorcerer may invoke to bind an opponent into a single, unbreakable contest. Its power is not destructive by nature but was authored to be drawn on as a conduit when a guild's oath is at stake.

rites.name: Eleinwen
rites.text: Eleinwen is a silver charm-stone worn by the wardens of the Hollow Choir in the Orierlae archives, granting its bearer one of two sharp workings: unravelling enchantments or hurling a crackling arc of storm-light. Its three years of study have shown it draws on the sleeping resonance of old bells, and it can scorch a stone bridge but never a cathedral.

rites.name: Venarlys
rites.text: Venarlys is a fractured crown-sigil of the Orierlae arcane courts, humming with borrowed lightning that scholars sell as a keepsake of rank. Its wielder can loose a ragged storm of unmade force that tears at whatever it touches, though the sigil itself grows brittle with every use.

rites.name: Venarlaerys
rites.text: Venarlaerys is a dormant arcane concept in the Orierlae omniverse, an ember of crystallised sorcery that stirs only when a caster names it aloud. Its earliest scholars recorded that it could unmake a single target with a corrosive burst, yet most of its power lies in what it leaves behind.

rites.name: Venirerleth
rites.text: Venirerleth is a sealed rite-name for a concept of borrowed beastly sinew, pursued by Arcane practitioners of the sixth age who graft a single animal's endurance onto their own frame. Its practitioners describe it less as a power than as a long agreement with a creature that never quite leaves.

rites.name: Ilyirwen
rites.text: Ilyirwen is a sentient crystalline tide-moth born in the luminous vaults of Orierlae during its sixth age, whose wings shed glowing shards that thicken into a protective carapace along its ribs. It drifts between the arcane spires, guiding lost travelers by the hum of its layered plates.

rites.name: Oriimeneth
rites.text: Oriimeneth is a concept-born arcane current in Orierlae, a shimmering thread of meaning that stirs when a sealed pact is spoken aloud in the old tongue. It cannot act on matter directly and instead rearranges the obligations that bind a place, so its strength is measured in how much it can unmake a vow's hold.

rites.name: Oriellimae
rites.text: Oriellimae is a shimmering arcane sigil-current that drifts through the Orierlae reaches, pulsing with the memory of a dead star's last breath. Within the Arcane realm of the sixth era, it is said to be a conduit that gathers loose ambient magic and releases it in a single, devastating surge.

rites.name: Ilyenwen
rites.text: Ilyenwen is a silver-tongued concept of the Arcane realm in the Orierlae omniverse, born three ages into the sixth era as a discipline of pressing hearts and minds into agreement. Its wielders learn to shape a listener's resolve with a single well-chosen word, and the old schools teach that such words can also crack stone when spoken at full resonance.

rites.name: Miinnarla
rites.text: Miinnarla is a concept of resolve woven into the arcane veils of Orierlae, a shield of unbroken will that steadies the mind against enchantment and terror. In the E6 age, scholars in the powers of the realm describe it as a lattice of calm laid over the thoughts of those who bear it.

rites.name: Alaira
rites.text: Alaira is a three-year-old arcane sentinel of the E6 era in Orierlae, whose translucent fins unfurl like living sails to cushion her fall and carry her gliding over the glassy canopy of the Thessaly reefs. Though she is young, her fins can channel a surge of stored tide-light that scorches the air around her when she dives from the highest spires.

rites.name: Oriamora
rites.text: Oriamora is a binding-cord of tensile sigils that the Orierlae mages weave into the soles and palms of climbers, letting them advance up sheer surfaces as swiftly as they cross level ground. Its wearers scale cliffs and spires at the same brisk pace they walk, though the sigils fade if the wearer's hands go unwashed of chalk-ash for a day.

rites.name: Ilyareimeth
rites.text: Ilyareimeth is a concept of arcane gill-sorcery, a quiet art that draws the breath of water through the skin of its practitioner. In the Orierlae cycle of the sixth era it marks the youngest school of the Arcane realm, still learning how far its tides can be bent.

rites.name: Eliorla
rites.text: Eliorla is a spirit-scholar of the Orierlae sky-archives, a being of quiet lamplight who catalogues the fading memories of dead stars. Within the archive vaults she can kindle a sealed moment back into full flame, though the cost is always paid in her own remembered years. Her long vigil has taught her that some silences are deliberate and should be left unbroken.

rites.name: Silarinwen
rites.text: Silarinwen is a tidal-rune of the Orierlae Arcane age, a conduit that binds the drift of deep currents into a slender coil of breath and grasp. Its wielders draw ocean-weight into their reach and breathe through liquid as easily as air. It was first recorded in the third age of the old lantern-courts.

rites.name: Nuillerora
rites.text: Nuillerora is a sealed resonance of the Arcane realm in Orierlae, a concept that lets its bearer draw breath from both open air and drowning depths alike. Its tide-stilled currents move through any medium at the same ease, so swimming and striding feel identical to it. Scholars of the third age regard it as a quiet lesson that boundaries between elements are only habits of the flesh.

rites.name: Lyilys
rites.text: Lyilys is a quiet current of resolve woven into the Arcane realm of Orierlae, granting its bearer a steadiness of mind against confusion, dread, and coercion. In the sixth era, scholars of the Vaelmere Concordance cite it as the reason certain wardens could hold their ground against illusions that broke whole armies.

rites.name: Alailae
rites.text: Alailae is a dormant mnemonic craft of Orierlae's Arcane realm, in which a practitioner draws a thought from the skull and shapes it into a solid, hand-sized object that can be held and passed to others. Its practitioners are few and its records are sparse, and it is typically regarded as a parlour art rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Coles
rites.text: A vast current of unseen essence runs through the entire world, quietly saturating every living thing and gently shaping its nature. Its workings are both visible and hidden to those who dwell within it.

rites.name: Nasteonium
rites.text: A predefined token-like enchantment of the far-future kind, first set down on trial cards for testing. It serves as a basic building block that bends the rules of conjured forces.

rites.name: Taulles Rollisor
rites.text: A practice that lets a bearer reshape the hourglass marks borne by their tokens. Its use bends the flow of accumulated moments, changing how long each token lingers.
